$comment: The room's MCP tools, written once: the plugin serves them and the evals' stand-in shows the same text. Placeholders: {{signals}} (signals.json), {{keep_log_days}} (settings.json), {{rotate_k}} and {{mail_chars}} (policy room.params). callers: "any" seat, "spawners" (roles the workflow lets create seats) or "room" (roles the workflow puts at home in the room); the plugin refuses the rest. Every seat is listed every tool, so a description names no role above a project.

seatwork_mail.description: Mail seats of your room; it is delivered between a recipient's turns and kept in the project's mail store. Answer a mail with `reply_to`. Start a thread with `to`; a seat with no seat under it may leave `to` out and writes to its owner. A body past {{mail_chars}} characters is shown cut, with the path of the file that holds all of it. A CANDIDATE, REVIEW or DONE to your owner is your turn's report: it is delivered when your turn ends, and your final message is not mailed again. `STOP`, to one seat you launched or one below it, ends its running turn and every running turn under it at once, and each reads your text next; use it when the work must not go on. The answer is JSON; a refusal is {"error": {code, message, retryable, fix}}.

to.description: `owner`, a seat you launched (its id, the start of its id, or its title), several of them, or `team`: every open seat under you, which reads it with its next mail. Omit with reply_to.

cc.description: Seats that get a copy to read; it starts no turn of theirs.

reply_to.description: The id of the mail you answer; the answer goes to its sender and joins its thread.

subject.description: Short; opens with one of the room's signals: {{signals}}.

body.description: Self-contained: the recipient may read it hours later.

needs.description: What you need back; `decision` says you are stopped until it comes.

thread.description: The work-store issue this mail is about; a reply keeps the thread of the mail it answers.

files.description: Paths the mail points at; each must exist.

key.description: Your own name for this mail: sent again with the same key and text, it stays one mail.

seatwork_inbox.description: Your mailbox. With nothing given: the mail held for you (what arrived while you were busy, and what starts no turn of its own), marked read. `id`: one mail whole. `thread`: a thread's mails, a line each. `view`: all you received, what you sent and how each delivery stands, what is owed (asks waiting for your answer, and yours waiting for one), or a search with `q`. You read your own mail and that of the seats under you.

id.description: One mail, with its whole body.

thread.description: An issue id, or the thread a mail names.

q.description: search: the words to look for.

signal.description: all, search: only mail whose subject opens with this signal.

since.description: all, sent, search: only mail after this ISO time.

bodies.description: thread: the mails whole, not a line each.

project.description: search, thread: another project's mail, by its folder or name, or all; for a seat that reads every project.

seatwork_projects.description: The project registry, one line per project Paseo knows: registered or not, name, root, whether its mission and law exist, its model table (default or custom), the Supervisor seat to use. Refused for seats that do not keep the registry.

seatwork_register_project.description: Register a project Paseo already has: writes its room marker and registry line, and its mission and model table when given; a seat the table names that the room lacks is set up first. Call again with `mission` or `models` to replace them. Refused for seats that do not keep the registry.

path.description: The project's root, or its name in Paseo (see seatwork_projects).

name.description: Registry name, letters digits dashes. Default: the Paseo name.

mission.description: What the project is for and what done looks like, a few lines of markdown.

models.description: Only the differences from ROOM_DIR/models.json, same shape; objects merge, lists and values replace, null removes a key. Omit to use the room's table.

seatwork_unregister_project.description: Take a project out of the registry: no seat of the room starts in it after that. Its `.seatwork/` files stay, and seatwork_register_project brings it back. Refused while a seat of the project is open, and for seats that do not keep the registry.

project.description: The project's registry name, or its root.

seatwork_room_stats.description: What the mail log shows for the last `days`, per project and signal (candidates accepted or rejected, reopen requests conceded or held, decisions escalated, questions), then what each project's seats used per role, as their agent CLIs report it. Refused for seats that do not keep the registry.

days.description: Window in days, {{keep_log_days}} at most and by default.

seatwork_work.description: The project's work store: issues, what each waits for, who holds it. `do` names the one thing a call does. create: one issue, or a whole plan in `issues`, written all or none; each may carry a `key` and name its `parent` and `deps` by another's key. ready: open issues nothing holds back (no open blocker, blocked parent or open child), highest priority first. claim: take an issue; refused when another seat holds it or an open blocker of its own waits. blocked_by: a bare id blocks; `:parent-blocked` and `:child-open` only hold back from ready. note: a dated line of progress. depend: `id` waits for `on`. close: with `reason`, once its blockers and children are closed; the seat that holds an issue does not close it, its Owner does. Also show, list, update, comment, undepend, reopen. Answers are JSON; a refusal is {"error": {code, message, retryable}}.

id.description: An issue id, or enough of it after the prefix to name one issue.

issues.description: create: several issues in one write. Each has title and may have key, description, design, acceptance_criteria, write_scope, priority, issue_type, labels, parent, deps.

description.description: What is to be done and why, enough for a seat that sees nothing else.

acceptance_criteria.description: The checks that show it is done, a line each.

write_scope.description: The files or folders this issue may change; the plan view names ready issues whose scopes collide.

parent.description: create: the issue this one is a child of. ready: only what is under this issue.

deps.description: create: what this issue waits for: ids or keys, or {id, type}.

on.description: depend, undepend: the issue `id` waits for.

type.description: depend: blocks by default; discovered-from is for work found on the way.

status.description: list: filter. update: open, in_progress or deferred; closing is `close`.

assignee.description: list: a seat id, or `me`. update: a seat id, `me`, or null to free the issue.

defer_until.description: update: an ISO time before which the issue is not ready.

text.description: note, comment: the line to add.

reason.description: close: what was done, and the commit or the evidence.

if_revision.description: update: the revision you read; the write is refused when the issue has moved on.

unassigned.description: ready: only issues no seat holds.

force.description: close: close over open blockers or children.

seatwork_graph.description: The project's open issues as a graph; `view` names the reading. triage: what to do first, scored with reasons (what much work rests on, what closing frees, priority), and the blockers worth clearing first. next: the one issue to take now; only a claim reserves it. plan: groups no dependency joins, which can run side by side, with each group's ready issues and the pairs whose write scopes collide. blockers: from `id` down to what must close first. alerts: an issue held and untouched for long, one holding many back, issues that wait for each other.

id.description: blockers: the issue to start from.

limit.description: triage: how many recommendations (10 by default).

seatwork_safety.description: The room's guard. Every shell command and file write of yours is checked before it runs; a blocked one comes with a six-digit code. check: what the guard would make of `command`, without running it. grant: let a blocked command of a seat under you run once, by its `code` (codes marked for the person only the person grants). waiting: the codes of the seats under you that wait for a grant. ack: when the room sends your candidate back after its hand-in check, keep one finding on purpose: its `id` and the `reason`; your Owner reads both. council: how each member of the room's council has read turns over the last `days`. label: say whether a `[council]` finding about a seat under you was right: its `id` (the number after the member), `value` right or wrong, and the `reason`.

id.description: ack: the finding's id from the returned candidate. label: the council finding's number.

reason.description: ack: why the finding stays. label: why the finding was right or wrong.

value.description: label: whether the finding was right.

days.description: council: how many days back; 30 when not given.

seatwork_seats.description: The open seats under you, one line each: role, title, id; at work or at rest and for how long, waiting for a permission, failed, or waiting for the room's retry; context held and cost; the signal its last turn ended with; a Peer's rejections since its last ACCEPT; mail held for it. A seat past {{rotate_k}}K tokens of context is marked: each step rereads the whole context, so its next task belongs to a fresh seat.

seatwork_rotate.description: Replace a seat under you whose context has grown large (seatwork_seats marks it) with a fresh one that continues its work. At the seat's next rest the room asks it for a handoff, starts a successor on the same model with the brief in force and that handoff, hands it the seat's own open seats, and archives the old seat. You get one notice with the new seat's id; a seat that writes no usable handoff stays, and you are told.

agent_id.description: The seat to replace: one you launched, or one below it.

why.description: Optional: one clause the seat is told, such as its context size or the task ahead.

seatwork_adopt.description: Take over a seat handed to you: it then reports to you, its `to: owner` reaches you, and you may mail it. Allowed only for a role you may create, and only when its current owner is archived or sits in your own chain. Then mail it its brief and your disposition of its last signal.

agent_id.description: Id of the seat to adopt (from the handoff).
